cases.feature: Real Coding Agent terminal delivery to AWiki Me
cases.preconditions: An isolated non-production App identity, Skill Agent identity, coding-agent runtime, daemon, User Service, Message Service, and macOS notification permission are available on the same approved tenant.
cases.action: Send an ordinary final message plus completed, blocked, and action-required terminal statuses through the real CLI/daemon/service path while AWiki Me is foregrounded and backgrounded.
exactOracles: The Skill Agent conversation remains visible, foreground delivery stays quiet, and the matching ordinary final message does not produce a duplicate notification.
Background delivery renders one semantic macOS notification per run; restart/backfill does not replay an already accepted terminal outcome.
negativeChecks: Accepted-only service receipts, fake facades, an unexpected foreground banner, duplicate notification, hidden Skill Agent conversation, missing background banner, or manual observation without case attestation cannot pass.

cases.feature: macOS native notification authorization and banner
cases.preconditions: A macOS runner has an isolated AWiki Me Development bundle, controllable notification authorization, and Notification Center observation support.
cases.action: Authorize notifications, background AWiki Me, deliver one terminal event through the production notification facade, and inspect Notification Center.
exactOracles: The Development bundle is authorized and exactly one banner with the localized Coding Agent title/body is visible outside the App.
negativeChecks: Fake facade calls, API success without visible Notification Center evidence, duplicate banners, wrong bundle identity, or foreground-only Toast evidence cannot pass.

cases.feature: Coding Agent background terminal notification routing
cases.preconditions: Flutter desktop can launch the authenticated fake-bootstrap AWiki Me shell without backend credentials.
cases.action: Background the App lifecycle and inject a completed awiki.agent.status.v1 update through the App realtime boundary.
exactOracles: The structured terminal status reaches AppShell and calls the system-notification facade exactly once with the localized completion content.
Background terminal feedback does not render an in-App Toast.
negativeChecks: A missing or duplicate system-notification call, wrong localized content, or any background in-App Toast fails the case.

cases.feature: Android EMAS direct-message product delivery
cases.preconditions: A dedicated authenticated AWiki Me identity is active on a physical Android device, notification permission and EMAS registration can be controlled, and User Service, Message Service outbox delivery, and EMAS are deployed on the approved test tenant.
cases.action: Upsert the authenticated Android installation, send one real direct message through Message Service outbox and EMAS, exercise foreground, background, terminated-process tap, WebSocket-plus-Push convergence, offline retry recovery, and finally logout.
exactOracles: User Service records one active installation bound to the authenticated account and the Android EMAS registration without exposing credentials or a full provider device identifier.

Foreground Push for the current account and same visible conversation commits and projects the direct message without a system notification or global App toast; when scrolled up, only the existing in-chat new-message affordance appears.

Foreground Push for the current account while another conversation or page is visible commits and projects the message, updates recents and unread state, and produces no Toast, Banner, or system notification.
A missing or mismatched opaque target fails open to provider presentation without exposing a raw DID or conversation identifier.
Background delivery renders exactly one EMAS NOTICE for the message.
A terminated-process notification tap starts Core sync and opens only the exact conversation matched from the newly committed message.
WebSocket and Push convergence produces one committed canonical message and one presentation outcome.
While offline, the pending Push event remains unacknowledged; after connectivity returns, successful sync and routing acknowledge it.
Logout disables the active installation, and a later send excludes the old DID installation from delivery.
negativeChecks: Provider API success, outbox done state, fake-client callbacks, duplicate Core messages, duplicate notifications, acknowledgement before successful sync and routing, wrong-conversation navigation, retained delivery after logout, or old-DID delivery can never pass.

cases.feature: Android EMAS physical-device registration and delivery
cases.preconditions: A Nubia P0110, or an explicitly named equivalent physical Android device, has an isolated AWiki Me build, resettable notification permission, controllable background and terminated-process state, and access to the configured EMAS application.
cases.action: Deny notification permission, recover it through Android settings, register with EMAS, and deliver notifications while the App is backgrounded and after its process is terminated.
exactOracles: Permission denial is observed before settings recovery, and Android settings recovery enables the subsequent visible notification path.
EMAS registration is proven with non-sensitive provider DeviceId suffix evidence only; the full identifier and all credentials remain absent from evidence.
The physical device receives the background notification and the terminated-process notification, and the terminated-process tap reaches the App open path.
negativeChecks: Provider API success, Message Service outbox done state, a fake facade, callback-only evidence without a visible notification, emulator-only evidence, or an unnamed substitute device can never pass.

cases.action: Provision one unique production scope item, terminate the test App process, launch a separately built process to reopen it, reject duplicate create, then delete it in a third process.
exactOracles: The gate builds awiki_im_core once before all App phases, validates arm64 and x86_64, and keeps Podfile.lock stable across the three Release builds.
The provision process creates revision 1 only in the production service.
The independent reopen process reads the same revision and createExclusive reports already-exists.
The cleanup process deletes the unique item and confirms missing.
negativeChecks: Native dependency preparation failure is reported before Keychain behavior; ad-hoc identity, dev-service access, restart read failure, silent replacement, or cleanup failure fails the release gate.

cases.feature: Current credential deletion across idle Patch and cold restart
cases.preconditions: A real native Core identity is active in an isolated App state root, the committed conversation Patch stream is attached and idle, and the runner can launch a third independent Flutter process against that same root.
cases.action: After the normal cold-restart conversation assertions, delete the current credential while the conversation Patch stream is idle; then start another Flutter process against the same App state root.
exactOracles: Deletion completes without waiting for presentation-stream cancellation, the native identity is absent, the active identity is not restored after cold start, and onboarding is visible without a persistent loading mask.
negativeChecks: A hanging Patch cancellation, retained native identity, retained active pointer, automatic relogin, same-process-only reopen, or persistent busy/loading state fails.

cases.feature: Canonical conversation cold-process restart
cases.preconditions: The runner can launch two independent Flutter integration-test processes against one isolated App state root and one attested x86_64 build.
cases.action: Phase A creates Direct/Group conversations, messages, unread state, and cached Profiles; Phase B starts a new Flutter process and restores only persisted state.
exactOracles: The second process restores Persona/Group semantic exact-one, exact message order, unread state, and cached first-visible names without reusing in-memory providers.
negativeChecks: Same-process Widget rebuild, duplicate/lost rows, unread drift, message replay, Handle/DID flash, changed native content hash, or a different state root fails.

cases.feature: Cold restart closes a message gap committed while Patch subscription is unavailable
cases.preconditions: Phase A has a real bound App/Core session, the runner can stop realtime and launch a distinct Flutter process against the same isolated state root, and the CLI peer is independently authenticated.
cases.action: Pause Phase A, stop realtime, destroy its App ProviderContainer and native bootstrap, prove Patch/sync providers are unavailable, then commit one Direct message from the CLI and start Phase B normally.
exactOracles: The gap message is accepted by the real backend only after Phase A realtime and its Patch/recovery coordinator container are destroyed.

Before Phase B mounts the App, its canonical local timeline lacks the gap; the distinct process then proves subscribe-reset-sync startup order and projects the gap exactly once alongside the pre-existing timeline.
negativeChecks: Leaving any old Patch/pull/recovery scheduler alive, committing before container disposal, finding the gap before Phase B startup, same-process rebuild, missing startup order evidence, lost/duplicate gap, or duplicate old rows prevents pass.

cases.feature: App shell smoke
cases.preconditions: Flutter desktop and debug native IM Core artifacts are available.
cases.action: Launch the real Flutter desktop app shim without backend credentials.
exactOracles: App shell and onboarding are visible exactly once.
The onboarding authentication entry is visible; macOS exposes the single phone, email, and identity-credential method selector.
On macOS, the phone OTP form submits the same-step handle and its tenant-qualified full handle.
The phone flow exposes one phone, Handle, and OTP form with a direct login/register action and no intermediate next step.
Unauthenticated realtime remains disconnected.
negativeChecks: A missing shell/onboarding/authentication-entry surface, a dropped OTP handle scope, a repeated Handle step, or an unexpected realtime connection fails the case.

cases.feature: Multi-conversation unread isolation and read clearing
cases.preconditions: The full remote awiki.info flow has one closed canonical Direct and one closed canonical Group.
cases.action: Receive two Direct messages and one Group message, restart, open Group, then open Direct.
exactOracles: Before opening, Direct unread is exactly 2, Group unread is exactly 1, and global unread increases by exactly 3.
Opening Group clears only Group and leaves Direct at 2; opening Direct then restores the exact baseline total with no rebound during the stability window.
negativeChecks: Wrong per-row/global count, clearing the wrong row, lost restart state, duplicate badge, or delayed unread rebound fails.

cases.feature: Canonical Direct conversation across App entries
cases.preconditions: The awiki.info peer has a nickname distinct from its Handle and DID, and the isolated App state contains no Direct row for that Persona.
cases.action: Create the Direct through identity lookup before the first message, then reopen it through recents, local conversation search, restart, and the visible Contact row.
exactOracles: Every App entry reuses the same peer-scope canonical conversation ID and peer Persona ID.
The empty pre-message conversation remains visible, then messages, preview, unread, and cached nickname stay attached to that single row across restart.
negativeChecks: A legacy dm:<DID> row, a second semantic row, a changed Persona/conversation ID, a lost empty row, or entry-specific title/state fails.

cases.feature: Canonical Group conversation across App lifecycle
cases.preconditions: The App creates a unique group on awiki.info through visible UI.
cases.action: Create the group, add the canonical peer, refresh members, restart the App shell, and send/receive the first messages.
exactOracles: Group creation produces exactly one conversation whose conversation ID, canonical Group DID, and wire thread remain aligned before the first message.
Adding a member, refreshing, restarting, and sending messages preserve that same single Group row.
negativeChecks: A disappearing empty group, duplicate Group row, changed Group identity, member-add replacement row, or first-message-only resurrection fails.

cases.feature: AWiki Me new-device Join with CLI admin
cases.preconditions: The dedicated phone allowlist is enabled on awiki.info; AWiki Me and an exact-revision CLI admin use independent fresh native Core roots; purpose-bound OTPs are resolved through validated fixed argv; the CLI admin runs its production foreground listener with the dedicated file host-notification sink before Join starts.
cases.action: Bootstrap the existing CLI admin, start its real listener, start Join through the real AWiki Me onboarding UI, restart the App while Join is pending, require the CLI listener to emit the redacted im.device.join.requested event before reading the local Core projection or starting verification, compare the independently displayed six-digit SAS, approve through the foreground CLI as a member, and wait for AWiki Me to re-resolve authorization.
exactOracles: The independently bootstrapped CLI admin and App requester use distinct fresh native Core roots; the OTP-authenticated App request remains pending before the admin starts verification, an App restart restores that same pending session without persisting SAS, and the listener emits exactly the dedicated redacted Join wake before any admin mutation.
The App-visible and CLI-derived six-digit SAS match without recording either value, and the production foreground CLI contract approves the fixed member role without an admin-role choice.

Both Registries contain exactly two devices: AWiki Me is the current active member with management_ready false only after authoritative re-resolution, while the CLI remains the current active management-ready admin.
negativeChecks: A fake provider, copied state, static OTP, unsafe resolver argv, malformed SMS-error response, missing listener host wake, direct Message Inbox hydration, unapproved host-event fields, split claim or admin polling, missing pending phase, changed or terminal Join after restart, persisted SAS, mismatched SAS/session/device, non-foreground approval, retained terminal SAS, admin role, or server success without final Registry authorization prevents pass attestation.

cases.feature: AWiki Me admin-side approval defaults to member
cases.preconditions: The dedicated phone allowlist is enabled on awiki.info; the runner explicitly enables the E2E-only unattended UserPresencePort; AWiki Me and an exact-revision CLI use independent native Core roots; OTPs are resolved through validated fixed argv; the authenticated App runtime is connected before the CLI starts Join. SMS request delivery is 200-only unless the explicit operator staged-OTP flag and exact reviewed SSH resolver are used.
cases.action: Bootstrap AWiki Me as the ready admin, start an independent CLI Join request while the App is on its normal authenticated shell, wait for system_notification_changed to refresh the Core Join inbox and expose the global review entry, open that entry to start verification exactly once, compare the independently derived six-digit SAS, approve the fixed member role through exactly one test-scoped user-presence decision, and poll the new-device result.
exactOracles: The independently bootstrapped App admin and CLI requester use distinct fresh native Core roots; the OTP-authenticated request remains pending until the App receives its system notification, refreshes the typed Core Join inbox independently of general message sync, exposes the global review entry, and the user explicitly starts verification.

The App-visible and CLI-derived six-digit SAS match without recording either value, and exactly one E2E-only user-presence confirmation succeeds without changing the production LocalAuthentication implementation.

Both Registries contain exactly two devices: the joining protocol_device_id is the CLI current active member with management_ready false, while the original App device remains the unique current active management-ready admin.
negativeChecks: A production user-presence override, copied or non-fresh local state, static OTP, unsafe resolver argv, unapproved or malformed SMS-error response, Registry discovery, direct requestSync/refreshJoinInbox calls, pre-opening Devices to bypass the global entry, split claim or admin polling, repeated verification start, secret-bearing evidence, mismatched SAS, an enabled approval action before SAS confirmation, any admin-role control, a denied or repeated user-presence result, mismatched protocol_device_id, or an active-admin joining result prevents pass attestation.

cases.feature: Two isolated AWiki Me Apps complete member Join on one macOS host
cases.preconditions: The dedicated phone allowlist is enabled on awiki.info; the runner explicitly enables the E2E-only unattended UserPresencePort; the runner builds two Debug App bundles with distinct stable bundle identifiers, build directories, and fresh native Core state roots; OTPs are resolved through validated fixed argv.
cases.action: Launch and concurrently drive one admin App and one joining App, start Join through the joining App UI, require the authenticated admin runtime to expose the listener-delivered global review entry without test-side inbox refresh, explicitly start verification, compare both locally rendered SAS values only in the loopback coordinator memory, approve through exactly one test-scoped user-presence decision, and wait for both Registry projections.
exactOracles: Two real AWiki Me processes use distinct bundle identifiers, build products, and fresh native Core roots; the joining App remains pending without SAS until the admin user explicitly starts verification from the global Join review entry.

The two App-rendered six-digit SAS values match only inside the authenticated loopback coordinator, no SAS is written to config, logs, attestation, or reports, and exactly one E2E-only user-presence confirmation succeeds without changing the production LocalAuthentication implementation.
Both App Core Registries converge to exactly the same two devices: the original App remains the management-ready admin and the joining App becomes the current active rootless member.
negativeChecks: A production user-presence override, copied/shared state root, shared bundle or build product, fake Core, direct requestSync/refreshJoinInbox calls, pre-opened Devices page, implicit or repeated verification, persisted or reported SAS, mismatched SAS/session/device, approval before explicit SAS confirmation, denied or repeated user presence, admin-role joining result, or either Registry failing exact two-device convergence prevents pass attestation.

cases.feature: Joined AWiki Me device deletes its local credential and starts Join again
cases.preconditions: DEVICE-JOIN-E2E-004 has completed on two isolated real App processes, the joining App is the current active member, and its completed New Device Join journal belongs to the same local identity and protocol device.
cases.action: On the joining App, leave the completed Join page, open Settings, confirm Exit and delete current credential through visible UI, verify the completed local Join journal is retired, then reopen Join from onboarding.
exactOracles: Deleting the joined credential returns the real App to onboarding without affecting the admin App or remotely revoking either registered device.
The joining App Core no longer lists the completed New Device Join session that created the deleted local identity.
Opening Join again shows one fresh phone, Handle, OTP, and start-action form with no active Join, activation retry, completed-state projection, or device error.
negativeChecks: A fake Core, direct provider mutation, copied state root, retained completed Join session, DID-only match for another protocol device, stale Device joined page, activation retry, error banner, or missing fresh Join input prevents pass attestation.

cases.feature: AWiki Me Join restart and terminal-state convergence
cases.preconditions: AWiki Me has a non-terminal Join checkpoint in an isolated Core data root and the matching awiki.info Join session can be polled, cancelled, or allowed to expire.
cases.action: Restart AWiki Me during Join, resume from Core state, then exercise cancellation and expiration as separate isolated runs.
exactOracles: The resumed screen projects the same session without persisting SAS in App state, and cancellation or expiration reaches one terminal state without authorizing a device.
negativeChecks: A duplicated device, stale approval action, raw token or OTP in reports, a persisted SAS, silent retry authorization, or a false passed attestation fails.

cases.feature: AWiki Me management-device root import
cases.preconditions: An accepted Step 3 contract has established a management-ready AWiki Me admin and an independent CLI active member with management_ready false; both use fresh native Core roots and exact protocol device IDs, and the unattended suite uses the test-scoped user-presence port while production LocalAuthentication remains unchanged.
cases.action: Open Devices on the ready AWiki Me admin, select the exact eligible member, let Core prepare a safe recipient summary, complete exactly one E2E-only user-presence decision, stop the App sender flow at standard P5 accepted, then bring the CLI receiver online to import and complete readiness directly.
exactOracles: Before receiver completion, the exact recipient remains active member with management_ready false; no Init-only pending, sender waiting, or App-owned transfer state is projected.

The App displays only Core's safe recipient summary, delegates exactly one E2E-only user-presence decision without changing production LocalAuthentication, and treats the closed standard P5 accepted receipt as the end of the sender operation.

The CLI receiver imports the envelope, completes directly with User Service, and becomes active admin with management_ready true after fresh device auth and Registry convergence; Root control never appears in either product inbox.
negativeChecks: A wrong or ineligible target, caller-supplied message ID, old list/retry/pending state, a second user-presence action, treating accepted as receiver readiness, waiting for or emitting an imported ACK/Reply, root/control JSON in inbox or UI, Root bytes in logs/errors/reports, or management actions before Registry readiness fails.

cases.feature: Receiver-local root completion recovery
cases.preconditions: A future focused receiver fixture has already consumed one accepted Root P5 envelope and persisted receiver-local completion-pending state before process restart.
cases.action: Restart only the receiving device, let Core resume its local HTTPS completion coordinator, obtain fresh device auth, read Registry once, and promote the already sealed pending root after authoritative admin-ready convergence.
exactOracles: Receiver-local recovery is idempotent across response loss, produces one readiness transition, projects ready only from fresh auth plus Registry, and promotes the pending root without any sender participation.
negativeChecks: Sender retry, a second user-presence prompt, an imported ACK/Reply, public original-message-ID retry semantics, duplicate readiness generation, a second App-owned state store, false ready before Registry, or raw transport error text fails.

cases.action: Read the first group page with limit one, retain its opaque cursor, and explicitly request the next page.
exactOracles: The first page has one item, has_more and a non-empty opaque cursor; the explicit next request returns a distinct stable group projection.
negativeChecks: Offset pagination, cursor parsing, automatic unbounded collection, duplicate items, or fake service data fails.

cases.feature: AWiki Me permanent device revoke
cases.preconditions: The same isolated awiki.info identity has two active management-ready devices after encrypted root import; the current AWiki Me device is a ready admin, and the unattended suite uses the test-scoped user-presence port while production LocalAuthentication remains unchanged.
cases.action: From the real Devices page, select the non-current device, accept the visible destructive confirmation, complete one fresh E2E-only user-presence decision, and wait for the authoritative Registry projection.
exactOracles: The target becomes revoked and loses its destructive action only after the Core mutation and Registry refresh, while the current AWiki Me device remains the active management-ready admin.
negativeChecks: Self revoke, revoking the final ready admin, cancellation, missing or repeated user presence, button-only success, an active target after refresh, or internal proof/version/key material in UI or evidence fails.

cases.feature: AWiki Me same-DID second-device MLS lifecycle
cases.preconditions: A real AWiki Me owner device and an independently initialized CLI member device use distinct fresh native Core roots against audited awiki.info P6 v2 endpoints.
cases.action: Create a required-E2EE group in AWiki Me, join the CLI as the same DID, run production App MLS reconciliation, consume Welcome on the CLI, then exchange future group text and one group attachment.
exactOracles: Before Welcome, the independent CLI root reports missing local MLS state and cannot see the App pre-Welcome application.
The App visibly projects preparing during production reconciliation and ready only after Add, Commit, and Welcome converge.
Future secure group text travels App-to-CLI and CLI-to-App exactly once.
One CLI group attachment object is projected once and decrypts to the exact plaintext in AWiki Me.
The same DID remains one owner business member throughout the second-device lifecycle.
negativeChecks: Copied native state, pre-Welcome history, stale ready during reconciliation, duplicate messages or business members, wrong attachment bytes, or MLS control/private fields in App or CLI public projections fails.

cases.feature: AWiki Me exact-device MLS revoke convergence
cases.preconditions: The App owner and independent CLI endpoint are active devices of one DID and have distinct MLS state in one required-E2EE group.
cases.action: Revoke the CLI device through the real AWiki Me Devices UI, wait for the exact Remove and Commit convergence, then send a future secure group application from the surviving App device.
exactOracles: The selected CLI device is authoritatively revoked and its exact MLS endpoint is removed.
The surviving App endpoint visibly reports ready only after Remove and Commit converge.
The revoked CLI endpoint is rejected at authorization before it can retrieve future group data.
The App continues secure group messaging while the DID remains one owner business member.
negativeChecks: Removing the surviving App endpoint or DID business membership, stale ready before removal convergence, recreating the revoked endpoint, future CLI access, duplicate messages, or MLS private fields in UI/evidence fails.

cases.feature: AWiki Me default device entry and independent security gates
cases.preconditions: Flutter desktop and debug native IM Core artifacts are available; no backend, OTP, CLI peer, or pre-existing identity is used.
cases.action: Open one temporary Storage Scope through production AppBootstrap/native Core, verify the default device-management composition, and open the public onboarding Join entry without submitting an OTP.
exactOracles: The launch uses a real Storage Scope ID, and the temporary App root is deleted after native runtime disposal.
With default configuration the production device-management and root-transfer adapters plus the public Join entry exist; the gated group-encryption adapter is absent.

The public entry opens the real Handle/phone/OTP Join form without exposing root transfer before authorized-member eligibility and explicit user presence; revoke and Direct/Group E2EE rollout gates remain closed, and Handle Recovery has no executable V1 flow.
negativeChecks: A reused/copied Core root, fake provider, backend-dependent oracle, a missing Join entry, root-transfer execution from the public form, hidden enablement of a gated capability, OTP submission, or any claim that remote Join/SAS/Root/Recovery passed fails the case.

cases.feature: Two joined AWiki Me Apps converge the same account Agent inventory
cases.preconditions: Two isolated macOS App processes complete member Join against awiki.info; the functional App-pair suite uses an E2E-only user-presence provider and starts one real local Daemon with Codex and Claude Code drivers.
cases.action: Open the Agents workspace on the joining App before the admin App installs the Daemon and creates one Codex plus one Claude Code runtime Agent, then wait only on the joining App provider/UI convergence path.
exactOracles: Both Apps project the exact same Daemon DID and Handle from the account-level User Service Agent Inventory.
Both Apps project the exact same Codex and Claude Code runtime DIDs, Handles, runtime kinds, and parent Daemon DID.
The joining App renders both runtime display names without the test directly invoking its inventory refresh after creation.
negativeChecks: A copied App/Core root, a second Daemon installation, a test-side inventory refresh after runtime creation, duplicate Agent rows, mismatched DIDs/Handles/parent topology, or either runtime name not becoming visible prevents pass attestation.
This case cannot attest macOS LocalAuthentication because the functional suite intentionally uses an E2E-only UserPresencePort.

cases.feature: A joined App sends a default-plain runtime Agent prompt that converges on the other App
cases.preconditions: Two isolated App devices share one joined account identity with the production-default Direct E2EE gate disabled; both Apps have converged the same real Codex runtime Agent and the joining App is displaying the normal Agents workspace.
cases.action: On the joining App, select the existing Codex runtime Agent, open its chat through visible UI, send one exact prompt through the real composer, then observe the exact canonical own-sync message on the admin App.
exactOracles: The joining App opens the already-converged runtime Agent chat and commits the exact prompt through the visible composer as a sent default-plain Direct message with the account DID and runtime Agent DID.
The admin App projects the same canonical conversation and exact message ID as isMine=true and visibly renders the prompt.
negativeChecks: Enabling Direct E2EE, calling MessagingService directly on the joining App, creating a test-only conversation, duplicate content, canonical ID mismatch, wrong sender or receiver, failed send state, missing own-sync semantics, or a non-visible admin-App message prevents pass attestation.

cases.feature: Direct messages sent on either joined App converge as own-sync on the other App
cases.preconditions: Two isolated App devices share one joined account identity with the production-default Direct E2EE gate disabled, and an independent fresh CLI identity is available as the remote peer.
cases.action: Send one exact Direct text from the admin App to the CLI peer and observe it on the joining App, then send a second exact Direct text from the joining App through the same canonical conversation and observe it on the admin App.
exactOracles: The admin App commits exactly one sent message with the account DID, peer DID, exact content, canonical message ID, and canonical conversation ID.
The joining App projects the first message as one canonical isMine own-sync message and renders it in the selected conversation.
The joining App signs and commits a second default-plain outbound message with its own joined-device signing key, the same account DID, and canonical conversation ID.
The admin App projects the second message as the exact canonical isMine own-sync message and renders it under the same conversation.
negativeChecks: A direct provider refresh that manufactures either conversation, duplicate body delivery, canonical ID mismatch, wrong direction, wrong peer conversation, missing own-sync semantics, or a non-visible bubble prevents pass attestation.
A joined-device outbound rejected because its Origin Proof keyid does not match its device signing private key prevents pass attestation.

cases.feature: A remote Direct reply converges on both joined Apps
cases.preconditions: The default-plain two-App own-sync case has established the canonical peer conversation and the independent CLI peer can send an ordinary Direct message.
cases.action: Send one exact default-plain reply from the CLI peer and observe the same canonical incoming message on both App device histories plus the joining App conversation list and visible timeline.
exactOracles: The admin App receives the exact CLI reply with the CLI DID, account DID, canonical reply ID, sent state, and isMine=false.
The joining App updates the same peer conversation preview without creating a second conversation.
The joining App receives the exact incoming reply with the same canonical ID and renders it in the already-open timeline.
negativeChecks: Unexpected secure-mode activation, duplicate reply delivery, canonical ID mismatch, wrong direction, a second peer conversation, only one App receiving the reply, or a non-visible reply prevents pass attestation.

cases.feature: Two online joined AWiki Me replicas converge ordinary Direct messages through sync v2
cases.preconditions: Two isolated App devices share one joined account identity, AWIKI_SYNC_V2_READ is enabled for the functional App-pair suite, Direct E2EE remains disabled, and an independent CLI identity is available as the remote peer.
cases.action: Keep both Apps online, send ordinary Direct messages from each App to the CLI peer, then send one ordinary reply from the CLI peer while both App runtimes consume WebSocket only as a pull trigger.
exactOracles: The admin App outbound message is projected exactly once as outgoing on the joining sibling device.
The joining App outbound message is projected exactly once as outgoing on the admin sibling device.
The same incoming CLI reply is projected exactly once on both online App devices under the same canonical conversation.
negativeChecks: A raw realtime payload directly writing list, timeline, Group state, or notification truth; duplicate event/hint rendering; wrong direction; canonical conversation drift; secure-mode activation; or only one online device receiving the reply prevents pass attestation.

cases.feature: A newly joined AWiki Me replica bootstraps at the current ordinary-message tail
cases.preconditions: Before Device Join begins, the existing admin App commits one ordinary Direct message to an independent CLI peer; the joining App uses a fresh isolated Core root and AWIKI_SYNC_V2_READ is enabled.
cases.action: Complete member Join, allow the joining App startup sync to finish without test-side cursor or sync calls, prove the pre-Join message is absent, then send one post-Join message through the existing App.
exactOracles: The ordinary pre-Join message is committed and visible on the existing App before the new replica is authorized.
The joining App completes bootstrap without exposing the pre-Join conversation or message.
A post-Join ordinary message becomes visible exactly once on the joining App, proving bootstrap did not disable future delta.
negativeChecks: Supplying cursor zero, account, device, replica classification, recovery token, or a test-side sync call; receiving any pre-Join message/history; failing bootstrap; or missing/duplicating the post-Join message prevents pass attestation.

cases.feature: A read watermark committed on one joined App converges monotonically on its sibling App
cases.preconditions: Two independently rooted Apps are authorized for the same account, both have completed sync v2 bootstrap, and an independent CLI peer can send one ordinary Direct message.
cases.action: Send one ordinary Direct message from the CLI peer, observe the unread projection on both Apps, open the canonical conversation on the joining App through visible UI, and let normal Core sync/realtime triggers converge the read watermark on the admin App.
exactOracles: Both Apps project the exact incoming ordinary message once and advance the same canonical conversation unread state.
Opening the joining App conversation commits a Core-owned read watermark without an App-owned checkpoint or direct read-state wire call.
The admin App eventually projects the same or higher read watermark and its unread count does not regress after reconnect or duplicate sync.
negativeChecks: A raw App read cursor, direct read-state payload, E2EE or MLS event, lower remote watermark, duplicate message, canonical conversation mismatch, or test-side projection mutation prevents pass attestation.

cases.feature: An existing AWiki Me replica resumes through Core-owned bounded compact recovery
cases.preconditions: The joining App is an already bootstrapped sync v2 replica with an isolated persistent Core root; the admin App and CLI peer can create ordinary Direct traffic while that replica is offline; the reviewed fixed operator helper is explicitly enabled for the allowlisted test account.
cases.action: Take the existing joining App offline, create one ordinary Direct message and a read-state change, use the fixed operator-only helper to create a retention gap for that exact joined device, then resume it through normal App lifecycle/reconnect triggers and observe the single high-level syncNow recovery flow without supplying any recovery control to the App.
exactOracles: The coordinator transiently reports recovery-required/recovering or completes recovery within one Core syncNow chain, then returns to idle without exposing cursor, token, cutoff, or count.
Recent ordinary messages converge exactly once from the Core committed projection while previously available older local messages remain available.
Current read state converges independently of the ordinary-message recovery window, and a post-anchor ordinary Direct message arrives exactly once through the following delta.
negativeChecks: An invalid operator receipt, App recover API, App-supplied cursor/token/cutoff/count, full-history replay, deletion of older local rows, duplicate post-anchor delivery, raw Snapshot merging in Flutter, auth-revoked background retry, or any E2EE/MLS history prevents pass attestation.

cases.feature: A joined AWiki Me replica converges an ordinary message after every realtime hint is lost
cases.preconditions: Two isolated Apps share one joined awiki.info account, the admin App has completed sync-v2 bootstrap, an independent CLI peer is available, and the App's reliable HTTP sync remains enabled.
cases.action: Quiesce sync, pause the admin App and stop its realtime service, commit one ordinary Direct message from the CLI peer while no WebSocket can observe its hint, then resume through the normal App lifecycle.
exactOracles: The realtime service is stopped before the peer message is committed and the local timeline remains unchanged before lifecycle resume.
App resume starts the normal reliable HTTP reconciliation path and projects the exact canonical peer message once.
A repeated local timeline read keeps one projection with the same canonical message ID.
negativeChecks: Using a raw WebSocket payload as message truth, a test-side cursor or sync call, observing the message before resume, missing or duplicating the reliable projection, changing its canonical ID, or relying on Push prevents pass attestation.

cases.feature: An active AWiki Me device normally reconnects and pulls its disconnect gap exactly once
cases.preconditions: The joined admin App has an active non-revoked device session, a connected realtime transport, an initialized message-sync cursor, and an independent CLI peer.
cases.action: Perform a normal realtime stop, commit one ordinary Direct message during the disconnected interval, resume the App, wait for WebSocket reconnection, and observe reliable HTTP gap reconciliation.
exactOracles: The ordinary WebSocket disconnect completes without revoking the device and the active device reconnects successfully.
The message committed in the disconnect interval is obtained from reliable HTTP reconciliation.
The canonical post-reconnect message is projected exactly once and remains exact-one on a repeated read.
negativeChecks: Treating revoked reconnect denial as normal reconnect evidence, changing device identity, direct projection from a hint, failing to reconnect, missing the disconnect gap, duplicate projection, or Push-based recovery prevents pass attestation.

cases.feature: Bound App startup establishes committed Patch readiness before reliable pull
cases.preconditions: A freshly joined App has a real native Core root, stable account binding, tail-only bootstrap, and the production committed conversation Patch stream.
cases.action: Complete normal App activation, inspect the product-owned payload-free startup ordering observation without calling the barrier from the test, receive the first post-Join sibling message, then repeat reliable HTTP sync.
exactOracles: The normal bound startup records Patch subscription start, committed reset readiness, and first reliable sync start in that strict order without a test-owned barrier call, cursor, or projection.
The first post-startup committed sibling message appears exactly once and a repeated reliable pull keeps exactly one canonical message.
negativeChecks: A post-bootstrap test call to ensurePatchReady, unbound session, test-owned checkpoint, direct cache write, missing or reordered startup observation, duplicate projection, or repeat full-refresh substitute prevents pass.

cases.feature: Post-recovery state exposes only typed product-safe sync diagnostics
cases.preconditions: An existing joined replica enters the reviewed real compact-recovery flow through normal App lifecycle resume.
cases.action: Resume through the Core-owned one-call compact recovery chain, allow the product coordinator to honor any Core-provided local-mutation retry deadline, then inspect only its typed diagnostics projection after the serialized reliable chain completes.
exactOracles: Core closes compact recovery within one syncNow call, any pending or scheduled local mutation is retried by the product coordinator at the Core-provided deadline, and the coordinator returns to a successful idle state without requiring Flutter to observe Rust-internal transient recovery phases.
Diagnostics expose a non-negative pending mutation count, closed dirty-domain/retry values, and last-success time.
The product refresh attempt and success sequences both advance after recovery, are equal, and mark the serialized observation current.
The E2E-safe diagnostics projection contains no cursor, epoch, account/device identifier, recovery token, message content, or payload field.
negativeChecks: A test-created allowlist map, stale diagnostics retained after refresh failure, reading raw SQLite, serializing IDs/cursors/content, accepting a negative count, or treating catalog text as runtime evidence prevents pass.

cases.feature: Same-DID revoked device is auth-fenced from later reliable sync
cases.preconditions: The joining App is an active real device for the same DID until the admin revokes that exact protocol device as the final shared-account action.
cases.action: Capture the exact joined-device account/auth binding, revoke that device, commit a new ordinary Direct message for the account, verify the original local binding remains in place, then trigger one normal reliable pull.
exactOracles: The real Registry mutation revokes the exact same-DID device after the E2E captured its original account and device-auth binding, before the post-revoke message is committed.
The revoked App does not project the post-revoke committed message before or after its subsequent reliable pull, and that pull ends in product auth fencing.
negativeChecks: Claiming direct stale-Patch injection, forging a binding, projecting the post-revoke message, allowing the revoked token to pull, revoking a different device, or running another shared-account case afterward prevents pass.

cases.feature: A runtime Agent added on one App converges to the joined sibling App
cases.preconditions: Two isolated macOS Apps are joined to the same awiki.info account, the Account State v1 target capability is declared, and the admin App controls one real local Daemon.
cases.action: Create Codex and Claude Code runtime Agents through the admin App product controller, then let the joining App reconcile only through its Account State coordinator.
exactOracles: The joining App consumes a higher Agent Inventory version and projects the exact Daemon/runtime parent topology.
Each added runtime DID appears exactly once with the expected Handle, runtime kind, and display name.
negativeChecks: Copied local state, a direct test-side cache write, duplicate Agent rows, mismatched parent topology, or attestation before the joining App projection converges prevents pass.

cases.feature: A runtime Agent rename converges independently across Apps
cases.preconditions: The same-account App pair already projects one exact active runtime Agent through Account State v1.
cases.action: Rename that runtime through the admin App product controller and reconcile the joining App.
exactOracles: The joining App Agent Inventory version increases and the same Agent DID retains its topology while exposing the exact new display name.
The joining App renders exactly one renamed Agent.
negativeChecks: A changed Agent DID, duplicate row, stale old name, direct cache mutation, or a name-only assertion without the higher Inventory version prevents pass.

cases.feature: Agent unbind converges as an inactive topology fact
cases.preconditions: Both Apps project the same active Claude runtime Agent under one real Daemon.
cases.action: Unbind the exact runtime through the admin App product controller, then reconcile the joining App.
exactOracles: The joining App durable Inventory snapshot retains exactly one inactive row for the unbound Agent DID at a higher version.
The joining App visible Agent projection removes that inactive Agent.
negativeChecks: Physical disappearance from the durable snapshot, a still-visible inactive Agent, duplicate rows, or inferring unbind only from the writing App prevents pass.

cases.feature: A real runtime delete completes on the writing App and converges to its sibling
cases.preconditions: Both Apps project the same active Codex runtime and the real Daemon reports an actionable control channel.
cases.action: Submit runtime deletion through the admin App controller and wait for the service-backed terminal reconcile before accepting sibling completion.
exactOracles: The admin App submits the real runtime delete and removes the target only after authoritative reconcile.
The joining App confirms terminal convergence for the exact Agent DID.
negativeChecks: Local optimistic removal alone, a Daemon command failure, a retained visible runtime, or treating a UI disappearance without sibling confirmation as delete success prevents pass.

cases.feature: A daemon-backed runtime delete archives an independent Agent across Apps
cases.preconditions: The admin App has created a third independent runtime through the real daemon and both Apps have converged it as active.
cases.action: Select that runtime in the product Agents controller and execute the normal daemon-backed runtime delete, whose authoritative remote lifecycle result is archived, then reconcile the sibling App.
exactOracles: The independent runtime is created through the product daemon path and is visible as active on the sibling before deletion.
The writing App submits the daemon-backed runtime delete rather than a test operator, direct storage write, or reuse of the separate Codex deletion.
The durable full Inventory snapshot contains exactly one archived row for the archived Agent DID at the higher version.
The visible Agents projection excludes the archived row.
negativeChecks: A test-only operator, direct storage mutation, reuse of the separate Codex deletion, physical row loss, visible archived Agent, duplicate row, or writing-side-only assertion prevents pass.

cases.feature: A Profile mutation converges through the independent Profile domain
cases.preconditions: Two isolated Apps share one stable account binding and both have completed Account State bootstrap.
cases.action: Update nickname and bio through the admin App Profile controller, then reconcile the joining App through Account State v1.
exactOracles: The joining App Profile version increases and its visible Profile projection matches the exact nickname and bio.
Agent Inventory and Device Registry versions remain unchanged by the Profile-only mutation.
negativeChecks: Timestamp conflict resolution, legacy unversioned Profile refresh, unrelated domain version amplification, stale Profile UI, or accepting only the writing-device response prevents pass.

cases.feature: One failed User domain does not block Profile or ordinary message convergence
cases.preconditions: The reviewed awiki-info-testing target declares Account State v1 and enables the fixed exact-account/exact-device one-shot Inventory failpoint with a bounded TTL; its managed User Service operator authorizes the ephemeral account through the active Handle phone binding and protected server-side test-phone digest allowlist.
cases.action: Arm one Inventory read failure for the joining device, mutate Agent Inventory and Profile, send an ordinary Direct message, reconcile once, then retry normally.
exactOracles: The first reconcile reports only Agent Inventory as failed while Profile advances and renders the exact new value.
The ordinary Direct message converges exactly while Inventory is failed, proving message sync is not blocked by a User domain.
The prior Inventory snapshot remains visible until a later retry pulls the higher version and clears the domain error.
negativeChecks: A wildcard or reusable failpoint, operator receipt used as a business oracle, cleared prior cache, blocked Profile/message sync, more than one failed domain, or pass before the normal retry converges prevents attestation.

cases.feature: Device Registry revoke converges to the active sibling and fences the revoked App
cases.preconditions: The admin and member Apps are joined, the admin is management-ready, real device revoke is enabled, and all other functional cases are complete.
cases.action: Load a fresh security Registry on the admin App, revoke the exact joined member with E2E-only user-presence, reconcile the admin display cache, then make the revoked App issue a product Registry request.
exactOracles: The still-active admin observes one exact revoked device in both the fresh Core Registry and a higher-version Account State display cache.
The revoked App's subsequent Registry request is rejected by generation/token fencing.
negativeChecks: Authorizing from the display cache, revoking the current admin, a different target device, no Registry version advance, successful use of the revoked token, or running further shared-account cases after revoke prevents pass.
